description: Take the Oriental Pearl Tower apart piece by piece in 3D, and read the story of Shanghai's 468-meter pink pearl: from farmland to the tallest structure in China, and the poem it was never based on.

people.name: Jiang Huancheng
people.role: Designed the tower for the Shanghai Modern Architectural Design Co.

hotspots.text: The lower great sphere, 50 meters in diameter, is the larger of the tower's two giant pearls. Eleven spheres in total ride on the three columns, from 50 meters down to decorative pearls of a few meters.
hotspots.title: The 50-meter pearl

hotspots.text: The upper great sphere, 45 meters in diameter, holds the sightseeing floor at 263 meters and the revolving restaurant at 267 meters. Between the two great spheres sits the 20-room Space Hotel.
hotspots.title: The 45-meter pearl

hotspots.text: The revolving restaurant turns a full circle at 267 meters, dining with a 360-degree panorama of the Huangpu and the Bund. Below it, at 259 meters, a glass-bottomed walkway tests visitors' nerves.
hotspots.title: Dinner at 267 meters

hotspots.text: The Space Module at 350 meters is the highest of the tower's fifteen observatory levels. Above it only the antenna continues, to the 468-meter tip.
hotspots.title: The Space Module

hotspots.text: The broadcast antenna transmits television and radio for some 30 Shanghai stations. In the early hours of 13 April 2010, after thunderstorms, the antenna caught fire; firefighters put it out.
hotspots.title: The antenna

hotspots.text: At night the tower runs bright LED illumination sequences, and its pink pearls glow over the river. The lighting made it the defining image of Pudong's skyline through the 1990s and 2000s.
hotspots.title: The night lighting

intro: In 1991 the tower's site was farmland. Three years later Shanghai had the tallest structure in China: eleven pink pearls strung on three concrete columns, 468 meters of 1990s futurism. This is the story of the Oriental Pearl Tower, and the poem it was never designed around.
page_title: Oriental Pearl Tower: Exploded 3D Model and History | Architectural Atlas

sections.body:
When construction began in 1991, Pudong was still largely farmland across the Huangpu from the Bund. Shanghai needed a television tower, and architect Jiang Huancheng of the Shanghai Modern Architectural Design Co. gave the city something far stranger than an antenna mast: three 9-meter concrete columns rising 350 meters, carrying eleven spheres of graded sizes like pearls.

The two great spheres, 50 and 45 meters in diameter, hold the observatories, the sightseeing floor and the revolving restaurant. The top sphere, 14 meters across, carries the Space Module at 350 meters. The antenna continues to 468 meters. Completed in 1994 and opened to the public in 1995, it was the tallest structure in China and all of Asia, and it stayed that way until the Shanghai World Financial Center passed it in 2007.
sections.heading: Pearls over farmland

sections.body:
The tower's design is routinely attributed to a line from Bai Juyi's Tang Dynasty 'Pipa Song,' about pearls big and small falling on a jade plate. It is a lovely story, and the designer says it is not true. Jiang Huancheng has stated plainly that the poem was not in his mind when he designed the tower; it was the chief of the jury board who remarked that the design reminded him of the verse.

What is true is that the tower became the symbol of the new Pudong almost overnight. It hosted the Chinese Live Earth concert on 7 July 2007, survived its 2010 antenna fire, and was listed as a Shanghai cultural relic protection unit the same decade it stopped being the tallest thing in China.
sections.heading: The poem that was never the plan

sections.body:
Transformers: Age of Extinction (2014) moved its production to China in a big way, filming in Hong Kong and Shanghai with Chinese stars and Chinese financial partners. The Shanghai skyline sequences use the city's towers as backdrops, and the Pearl Tower's unmistakable pink-sphere silhouette appears among them: the film needed an instantly readable 'Shanghai,' and the tower is what that looks like.

The tower's stranger screen legacy is the one it almost had. When Skyfall (2012) sent Bond to Shanghai, the celebrated silhouette fight was shot at Pinewood Studios in London, with the Shanghai skyline added digitally afterward. The tower that defines the real skyline never stood on that set.

The myth worth retiring is the Bai Juyi story, repeated in nearly every guidebook: the pearls-and-jade-plate verse is a jury chairman's remark, not the architect's inspiration. The tower's real poetry is structural, eleven spheres that made a television mast into a landmark.

timeline.text: Construction begins in Lujiazui, Pudong, then still largely farmland.
The tower is completed at 468 meters; Jiang Huancheng's design for the Shanghai Modern Architectural Design Co.
Opened to the public; the tallest structure in China and Asia.
Hosts the Chinese Live Earth concert on 7 July; the Shanghai World Financial Center surpasses it as China's tallest.
The antenna catches fire after thunderstorms; firefighters extinguish it.
Transformers: Age of Extinction films in Shanghai with the tower in its skyline footage.
